newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent glides higher in quiet technical trade.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent glides higher in quiet technical trade.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures were slightly firmer on Monday after the market opened in what traders said was quiet technical-led trading.
August Brent was 10 cents a barrel firmer at 0929 GMT and stood at $17.95, while July gas oil was 75 cents a tonne up at $162.50.
"Now that OPEC is out of the way I am expecting a very quiet day," one IPE broker said.
A senior Venezuelan oil official said late on Thursday his country would export an average of 3.3 million barrels per day next year.

The figures contradicted statements by Venezuela's Minister of Energy and Mines Erwin Arrieta, who agreed on Wednesday at the OPEC meeting in Vienna to stick to Venezuela's official quota of 2.359 million bpd.
"This is not having any effect," the broker said. "It's not something we didn't know already."
Technical analysts said they were not expecting any great moves on Friday, but many were cautiously bearish.
"I wouldn't expect it to do anything great today. I think it will have a look at support at $17.70 and then fail.
But in the longer run I think it is going lower and I see $17.30 as a good level at which we might see some fund buying coming in."
This latter number lies adjacent to $17.32, the low point on the front-month continuation chart, reached on June 11.
